title: Blake Purchase’s 58-yard interception return helps Ole Miss pull away in 41–17 Egg Bowl win
excerpt: Mississippi State pulled within three early in the fourth quarter. Purchase returned an interception to the 1, setting up the first of three straight Ole Miss touchdowns.

paragraphs.text: Mississippi State was driving for a chance to retake the lead in Oxford when Blake Purchase intercepted a pass at the Ole Miss 41 and returned it 58 yards to the Bulldogs’ 1. One snap later, Trinidad Chambliss scored. A three-point game became a 27–17 Ole Miss lead with 10:30 left, and the Rebels went on to win Friday’s Egg Bowl 41–17.

The Bulldogs had taken a 10–6 lead into halftime. Fluff Bothwell scored on a 16-yard run in the second quarter, and Kyle Ferrie added a 42-yard field goal with 1:48 left in the half. Ole Miss had two Lucas Carneiro field goals and had yet to reach the end zone.

Ole Miss scored five touchdowns after the break. Chambliss found Horatio Fields from six yards out on the opening drive of the third quarter, and Joshua Dye ran in from the 4 for a 20–10 lead. Bothwell answered with a 12-yard touchdown catch five seconds into the fourth. That brought State within three before Purchase’s return set up the first of three unanswered Ole Miss touchdowns.

Chambliss threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to Michael Smith, and Dye scored his second rushing touchdown with 1:57 left. Chambliss finished with 237 passing yards, two touchdown passes and a touchdown run. Ole Miss has now won four straight against Mississippi State, its first four-game winning streak in the series since 1983–86.
